claims.text: The as-cast AlCoCrFeNi2.1 alloy has a dual-phase microstructure consisting of a disordered FCC matrix and B2 intermetallic precipitates.
The as-cast AlCoCrFeNi2.1 alloy exhibits high ductility.
Aging near 600°C produces a brittle state in AlCoCrFeNi2.1.
The brittle window occurs when the L12 long-range order parameter in the FCC matrix exceeds approximately 0.85.
Increasing L12 order maximizes the antiphase-boundary energy in the FCC matrix.
High antiphase-boundary energy suppresses dislocation cross-slip and promotes planar slip.
Coarsening of B2 precipitates changes B2/FCC interfaces from planar to jagged or serrated.
The jagged B2/FCC morphology develops through anisotropic interfacial-energy minimization.
Planar slip bands impinging on jagged B2/FCC interfaces produce dislocation pile-ups and localized stress concentrations.
The localized stress at interface serrations exceeds the cohesive strength of the interface before cross-slip can accommodate strain, causing interfacial decohesion.
At approximately 750°C, thermal energy lowers the L12 order parameter and consequently lowers the antiphase-boundary energy.
Aging near 750°C smooths B2/FCC interfaces or forms disordered transition zones along them.
Lower ordering and modified interfaces at 750°C restore cross-slip and ductility.
Elongation falls below 5% after aging at 600°C and recovers above 20% after aging at 750°C.
The brittle state will exhibit planar slip bands terminating at jagged B2/FCC interfaces.
The ductile state will exhibit wavy slip and dislocation penetration through or bypass of B2/FCC interfaces.
A serration amplitude greater than 50 nm is required for the interface to act as the proposed critical stress concentrator.
Cross-slip is active below an L12 order parameter of about 0.85, whereas planar slip dominates above it.

contradictions.description: The mechanism states that high L12 ordering and high APBE independently suppress cross-slip and produce planar slip, yet falsification rule (1) treats planar slip at a smooth interface as falsifying. Planar slip at a smooth interface would remain compatible with the stated ordering-to-slip mechanism; it would challenge only the necessity of jagged interfaces for fracture.

The hypothesis says APBE reaches a level that exceeds a critical stress for cross-slip, but APBE is an energy per unit area whereas critical cross-slip stress is a stress. These quantities cannot directly exceed one another without an explicit energetic-to-stress conversion model.
